claim: CPO (Contrastive Preference Optimization) improves LLM performance on complex reasoning tasks by an average of 4.3% without increasing inference time, compared to the base model.
falsifier: Apply CPO to a new LLM and benchmark on similar reasoning tasks; measure performance gain and inference time relative to the base model; the claim predicts a ~4.3% average improvement with no increase in inference latency.

conditions: training uses CPO with tree-search-generated preference data
evaluation on seven datasets across three LLMs
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLMs, datasets, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: CPO training–performance on complex reasoning principle
